back2basics.concept: HPV Vaccination and Cervical Cancer Prevention
back2basics.text: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is a virus that can cause cervical cancer in women. Vaccination against HPV is a preventive measure that protects individuals before they are exposed to the virus. Vaccines are typically given to adolescent girls to build immunity early. National immunisation campaigns use government health facilities and frontline workers to deliver vaccines safely and monitor adverse events. Digital platforms can support tracking and transparency in vaccination programs.

2026-11-21-pm-333e042f7b.deck: India has achieved a milestone by administering more than 1 crore doses of the HPV vaccine to 14-year-old girls under a national campaign launched in February 2026. This progress is significant for cervical cancer prevention and reflects strong government coordination and public confidence in preventive healthcare.

body.label: Campaign launch and target

body.label: MoU details
body.text: The Digital India BHASHINI Division and NIELIT signed a Memorandum of Understanding to collaborate on advancing multilingual AI applications, technology education, research, and capacity building under the BHASHINI for Seva/Sanchalan programme.

body.label: Focus on language barriers
body.text: The collaboration aims to reduce language barriers in technical education and digital learning by enabling access to technology knowledge and training in preferred Indian languages.

body.label: Integration and innovation
body.text: Both organisations will explore integrating BHASHINI's AI-powered language technologies into NIELIT's educational and training ecosystems, supporting multilingual access to learning resources and promoting AI-powered translation and speech technologies.

body.label: Inclusive learning environments
body.text: The partnership seeks to create inclusive and accessible learning environments where language does not constrain engagement with emerging technologies and technical subjects.

sections.heading: What is the BHASHINI and NIELIT collaboration about?

body.label: Healthcare applications
body.text: At the Global Digital Health Summit 2026, BHASHINI showcased multilingual AI applications supporting healthcare professionals through speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and translation technologies across institutions like AIIMS, JIPMER, and the Directorate General of Medical Services (Army).

body.label: Clinical workflow integration
body.text: BHASHINI's technologies enable voice-based documentation of clinical histories, prescriptions, and discharge instructions, facilitating doctor-patient communication across languages and simplifying clinical workflows.

body.label: Speech-to-text capability
body.text: The speech-to-text tool 'Shrutlekh' supports real-time multilingual transcription and translation, helping overcome language barriers in healthcare settings.

body.label: Impact on healthcare
body.text: These multilingual AI applications improve efficiency, accessibility, and inclusivity in healthcare delivery, reflecting the potential of India's indigenous language technology ecosystem.

sections.heading: How is BHASHINI advancing multilingual AI in healthcare?

body.label: Government initiatives
body.text: BHASHINI's work aligns with the Government of India's vision of a digitally empowered and technology-driven nation, contributing towards Viksit Bharat 2047 by making language an enabler rather than a barrier.

body.label: Capacity building focus
body.text: The collaboration with NIELIT and applications in healthcare demonstrate efforts to expand digital literacy, technical education, and skill development across linguistic groups.

body.label: Enhancing public services
body.text: Multilingual AI can strengthen delivery of institutional services and public-facing digital platforms, making them more accessible to citizens in their preferred languages.

body.label: Research and innovation

back2basics.concept: Digital Health Records and Ayushman Bharat
back2basics.text: Digital health records enable storing and sharing patient health information electronically for better continuity and quality of care. The Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) is a unique digital ID that links health records across healthcare providers, facilitating seamless access and management of patient data with consent. This supports evidence-based healthcare delivery and integration of various health services.

2026-11-21-pm-80f9d254e3.deck: The Union Health Secretary launched NCG VISHWAS, an AI-enabled patient education initiative by the National Cancer Grid, emphasizing linking cancer screening records with the Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) for continuity of care. This integration leverages India's digital health infrastructure to improve cancer awareness, screening, treatment affordability, and data-driven healthcare delivery.

body.label: Patient education initiative
body.text: NCG VISHWAS (Videos to Support Health, Wellness, Awareness and Self-care) is an AI-enabled patient education program covering breast, cervical, and oral cancers in multiple languages, providing reliable information on prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and long-term care.

body.label: Dissemination and reach
body.text: The initiative will be shared through the National Cancer Grid’s network of over 400 cancer centres and healthcare partners, including community health workers like ASHA and Anganwadi workers.

sections.heading: What is NCG VISHWAS and its purpose?

body.label: Digital health integration
body.text: Linking screening records with ABHA IDs under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission enables interoperable health records, supporting continuity of care across primary, secondary, and tertiary facilities.

body.label: Scale of implementation
body.text: Around 99 crore ABHA IDs have been created, with about 100 crore health records linked, facilitating longitudinal health records accessible with patient consent.

sections.heading: How does linking with Ayushman Bharat Health Account help?

body.label: Screening coverage
body.text: Over 153 crore screenings have been conducted for oral (37.1 crore), breast (17.4 crore), and cervical (9.7 crore) cancers at 1.87 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs across India.

body.label: Awareness and affordability
body.text: Awareness campaigns like Swasth Nari Sashakt Parivar Abhiyaan reached 11 crore footfalls, while financial support worth approximately ₹27,000 crore has been provided for cancer care under Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY.

sections.heading: What is the scale and impact of cancer screening under national programmes?

body.label: Collaboration and research
body.text: NCG encourages member hospitals to partner with the Pan-AIIMS Research Consortium to use patient-consented data for advancing cancer care and research.

body.label: Infrastructure strengthening
body.text: Efforts include expanding comprehensive primary healthcare packages, establishing Day Care Cancer Centres at district hospitals, technology-enabled radiology services, and strengthening oncology at 22 new AIIMS.

sections.heading: How does the initiative support cancer care and research?

2026-11-21-pm-a087b04c77.anchor: Separation of powers and social legal reforms

back2basics.text: The separation of powers divides government responsibilities into distinct branches to limit any one branch from exercising the core functions of another. The legislature makes laws, the executive implements them, and the judiciary interprets them. This principle ensures checks and balances in governance and prevents concentration of power.

2026-11-21-pm-a087b04c77.deck: The Supreme Court of India has asked the Union Government to consider legislation or awareness measures regarding marriages between close blood relatives. This development is important for understanding the separation of powers and social legal reforms in India.

back2basics.concept: Indus Water Treaty and SCO framework
back2basics.text: The Indus Water Treaty is a water-sharing agreement between India and Pakistan, governing the use of rivers originating in India and flowing into Pakistan. The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) is a multilateral regional grouping that includes India and Pakistan as permanent members, providing a platform for dialogue and cooperation among member states.

2026-11-21-pm-a7538492db.deck: India reaffirmed its unchanged position on the Indus Water Treaty (IWT) during the visit of Pakistan's Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik to the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Delhi in November 2026. This event marked a rare diplomatic engagement between the two countries following recent tensions, highlighting the complexity of bilateral water disputes within multilateral platforms.

back2basics.text: Diplomatic peace talks are negotiations between conflicting parties aimed at resolving disputes without further violence. They often involve compromises on territorial control, security guarantees, and political status. Such talks may include third-party mediators or hosts and require coordination among multiple stakeholders for a sustainable settlement.

body.label: Trilateral talks held
body.text: In November 2026, Russia, Ukraine, and the U.S. held two-day negotiations in Abu Dhabi hosted by the U.S., focusing on political settlement and humanitarian issues like prisoner exchange.

body.label: No major breakthrough
body.text: The talks failed to bridge the wide gap between Kyiv and Moscow, with positions remaining far apart on territorial and security issues.

body.label: Follow-up meetings planned
body.text: Subsequent discussions involving U.S., Ukrainian, and European officials are planned in Berlin to coordinate a European and Ukrainian stance on the peace process.

sections.heading: What happened in the recent Russia-Ukraine peace talks?

body.label: Divergent demands
body.text: Russia demands Ukraine withdraw from territories in Donbas, limit its military capabilities, and declare neutrality by giving up NATO ambitions, while Ukraine refuses territorial concessions and seeks Western security guarantees.

body.label: Prolonged conflict impact
body.text: Ukraine has lost over 20% of its territory, millions have fled, and the economy depends on European support, while its military relies on NATO supplies.

body.label: Shifting international support
body.text: Western unity supporting Ukraine is weakening, with some leaders seeking to reset ties with Russia and reestablish contacts with Moscow.

sections.heading: Why are the peace talks challenging?

body.label: Europe’s involvement needed
body.text: For the peace process to be meaningful, European countries must be brought to the negotiating table alongside Russia, Ukraine, and the U.S.

body.label: Geopolitical implications
body.text: The conflict and peace talks affect global security dynamics, influencing India’s foreign policy and its strategic interests in the Indo-Pacific region.

body.label: Diplomatic settlement as only way
body.text: Neither Russia nor Ukraine has a clear path to military victory, making diplomacy the only viable solution to end the war.
